titles.635: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — 'Adam sinned for all posterity': true as great harm; false as loco nostro
titles.636: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Scripture never says loco-sin; Christ truly satisfied / died / suffered in our place
titles.637: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — were we bound to sin so Adam would? unheard to sin as another's vadem
titles.638: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — did Adam take our law-keeping part to spare us? Away with such thoughts
titles.639: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — if Adam fulfilled the law loco posterorum, posterity would be free in their persons
titles.640: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC tip — only Adam & Eve then; he did not mean to sin in our place; cannot for non-consenters

latin.635: Minus etiam capio quae subnectis, cum Adamus peccavit, pro omnibus suis posteris peccavit. Si intelligis eum magno omnium posterorum malo peccasse, nihil verius. Hinc enim natum est vitium illud quod genus humanum invasit & morti addixit. Sed si intelligis eum loco nostro peccavisse, nihil dici potuit a te minus considerate.
latin.636: Nam neque id Scriptura dicit uspiam, & valde absurdum est. Satisfecit quidem loco nostro Christus iustitiae divinae: quippe nos enim tenebamur satisfacere. Moriendum erat omnibus nobis, ipse mortem loco nostro gustavit. Puniendi eramus omnes, ipse omnium loco passus est.
latin.637: Num igitur peccare tenebamur, ut nostro loco Adamus peccaret? Mihi quidem hactenus inauditum fuit peccare aliquem loco alterius tanquam eius vadem posse.
latin.638: Sed fortasse nostrae partes erant legem, tunc Adamo latam, tunc observare, atque adeo audire, memoriae mandare, intelligere, exequi. Adamus autem ut nos hac molestia levaret se suffecit in locum nostrum qui nostrum officium impleret, nostras partes ageret. Apage tales cogitationes.
latin.639: Profecto, si loco omnium posterorum Adamus legem illam implevisset, eius posteri ad eandem legem implendam ipsi in propriis suis personis non fuissent amplius obligati, quemadmodum quia loco nostro Christus iustitiae divinae satisfecit, non tenemur amplius ei satisfacere.
latin.640: Certe quemadmodum tunc temporis nulla erat in mundo persona humana praeter Adamum & Evam, sic nulla praeter eos duos persona humana aut poterat, aut debebat legi illi pro illo tempore parere. Neque vero Adamus ea mente peccavit ut loco nostro peccaret, neque, si mens ea ipsi fuisset, in cuiusquam potestate est loco alterius non consentientis peccare. Neque id naturae lex exigebat ut posterorum loco peccaret, neque Dei bonitatem & iustitiam decebat id efficere & constituere.

pass_a.635: Placeus splits Garrigues's 'Adam sinned for all posterity': true if it means great harm birthing the race's death-bound vice; false and careless if it means Adam sinned in our place (loco nostro).
pass_a.636: Scripture never says loco-sin for Adam, and the claim is absurd. Christ truly did what loco means—satisfy, die, suffer for us who were bound to those things.
pass_a.637: Were we obliged to sin so that Adam could sin in our place? Placeus says he has never yet heard that anyone can sin loco alterius as that person's surety (vadem)—sin-as-surety is not on the map.
pass_a.638: He floats then rejects the idea that our part was then to keep the law given to Adam, while Adam put himself in our place to do our duty and spare us the trouble. Away with such thoughts, he says.
pass_a.639: The Christ parallel cuts against Garrigues: if Adam had fulfilled that law in all posterity's place, they would no longer be bound to it in their own persons—just as Christ's satisfaction in our place frees us from satisfying again.
pass_a.640: Tip: only Adam and Eve then could or should keep that timed law. Adam did not intend to sin in our place; even if he had, no one can sin for a non-consenting other. Neither nature's law nor God's goodness and justice required or appointed such loco-sin. Tip before the missa/poena counter.

635: Still less do I grasp what you add: when Adam sinned, he sinned for all his posterity. If you mean he sinned to the great harm of all his posterity, nothing is truer. For from that was born the vice that invaded the human race and devoted it to death. But if you mean he sinned in our place, nothing less carefully considered could have been said by you.
636: For Scripture nowhere says that, and it is exceedingly absurd. Christ did indeed satisfy divine justice in our place—for we were bound to satisfy. All of us had to die; he tasted death in our place. All of us were to be punished; he suffered in the place of all.
637: Were we then bound to sin, so that Adam might sin in our place? For my part it has so far been unheard-of that anyone can sin in another's place as his surety.
638: But perhaps our part was then to keep the law then given to Adam—to hear it, commit it to memory, understand it, carry it out. And Adam, to relieve us of that trouble, put himself in our place to fulfill our duty and play our part. Away with such thoughts.
639: Truly, if Adam had fulfilled that law in the place of all his posterity, his posterity would no longer have been bound to fulfill the same law in their own persons—just as, because Christ satisfied divine justice in our place, we are no longer bound to satisfy it.
640: Certainly, just as at that time there was no human person in the world besides Adam and Eve, so no human person besides those two either could or ought to obey that law for that time. Nor did Adam sin with the mind of sinning in our place; and even if that had been his mind, it is in no one's power to sin in the place of another who does not consent. Nor did nature's law require that he sin in posterity's place, nor did it befit God's goodness and justice to effect and appoint that.

636.gloss: suffered in the place of all

635.choice: True as harm; false as loco nostro

638.choice: Adam did not take our law-duty to spare us

639.choice: Loco-fulfillment would free posterity like Christ

640.choice: Only A&E then; no loco-intent; no non-consenter
